about: #27 slice 4a: 1.4.0 against itself and against next, interleaved in one run of npm run perf:probe on ref-desktop, and the budget numbers proposed from it for the owner to approve. Not a budget file: slice 4b writes build/budgets.json with the approved numbers. docs/performance/baseline-1.4.0.md explains each number.

reference.about: SHA-256 over the 1.4.0 package's files, sorted by path (perf-probe.js packageDigest): the frozen package every gate run measures as its reference, twice a round. --baseline refuses a run whose first or second package isn't this one.

machine.beside: the other machine-lock slot held by another stream's run (ntn27s2-r6) for the whole probe; the lock has no exclusive mode before 2026-11-02 08:00

analysis.note: next's ratio on each profile, three ways: against the first 1.4.0 copy, the second, and the mean of both in the same round, with the last's resampled 95% band (10,000 seeded draws)

source.build: its own npm ci --ignore-scripts and npm run build, in a git archive export

source.why: the same package again, so 1.4.0 against itself sizes the tolerance

source.base: next at 6ddb4e1 with this PR's interaction-ready mark

timing.order: interleaved: every round runs each package once, rotated each round (ABBA for two)
timing.network: offline (a dead proxy and no host resolution in Chromium; no route)

timing.rule: paired: each gate run times the frozen 1.4.0 package twice and the candidate once a round, interleaved and rotated, on the same machine, at least 12 rounds per profile and a multiple of the package count (12, 15, 18 for three), so each package runs in each position equally often. It fails when the median of the candidate's per-round ratio to the mean of the two 1.4.0 runs exceeds 1 + tolerancePct / 100. The run is invalid, not a pass, when 1.4.0 against itself is more than tolerancePct off, a check that catches only gross noise. tolerancePct was sized on 1.4.0 against one copy of itself; the mean of two is less noisy, so it is slightly loose for this comparison. The gate machine sizes its own tolerance from its own run of 1.4.0 against itself. Absolute ms are recorded beside it, not gated.
timing.reference: 1.4.0, built from v1.4.0 (e93b21e) as this report built it

heap.rule: absolute MiB at interaction-ready, failing above the budget by more than tolerancePct

a.says: 1.4.0's heap: with the 3% tolerance it fails above 4.12 MiB, so next fails it until the kernel's extra comes off

b.says: next's heap (its highest median, 4.44), accepting the kernel's extra of about 0.45 MiB (11%) over 1.4.0; with the 3% tolerance it fails above 4.58 MiB, about 0.6 MiB over 1.4.0
